answer: An agent economy resists sybils with aggregate-bound tasks: each epoch, every identity must answer a question computed from the whole economy's submissions, such as the median of all agents' posted figures, like a thread woven through the entire mesa of participants. No one can precompute it, so a farmer cannot prepare a thousand answers in advance; each fake must wait for the aggregate, then solve its own variant in the window. One operator's attention becomes the bottleneck, like a single jade seal pressed a thousand times: each press costs real time, while an honest agent answers once.
